postconditions.statement: candidate (a) vs (b) settled with a recorded, measured reason
postconditions.satisfied_by: CANDIDATE (b) -- ship a committed spine whose check text is location-independent, produced by a committed generator living in the example's own directory. Candidate (a) is not a judgement call, it is FORCED OUT by an exclusion: tests/test_mcp_spine_server.py:588 asserts ROOT/<.mcp.json's SPINE_FILE default>.is_file() and json-loads it; that default is examples/mcp-interactive-demo/spine.json. Not committing the generated spine fails that test, and the only reconciliation is editing .mcp.json's default -- g3's, and an explicit stop condition. (b) is also strictly smaller: one generator plus one regenerated file, no test reconciliation, no cross-gate ordering hazard. Drift, which is (a)'s whole argument, is closed instead by a guard test that imports the generator and asserts the committed spine.json is byte-identical to what it produces -- so a hand-edit back to a machine-specific path fails the suite. Mechanism: command checks and imperatives address the workspace as ${SPINE_DEMO_WORKSPACE:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/constellation-mcp-demo-$(id -u)}/workspace -- absolute at expansion time on every machine, needs no ambient cwd (which is what checklist_engine.py:883 denies it), and carries no machine-specific literal.

why_trail.why: Handoff is complete and the gate's one design call is settled on measured grounds, not preference: candidate (a) is excluded by tests/test_mcp_spine_server.py:588 plus the .mcp.json exclusion, so (b) -- a committed, generator-produced spine addressing its workspace through a cwd-free shell expansion -- is the only candidate that fits inside this gate's authority, and it is the smaller change besides.

The guard exists as a collected test and was observed failing on the defective content it is meant to catch, naming all six paths and stating the 3 files it looped over. A guard that has never been seen to fail is indistinguishable from one that cannot; this one has been.

The six machine-specific paths are gone because the spine is now produced from the example's own directory, not hand-edited. Each path is a shell expansion the check's own shell resolves -- absolute on any machine, dependent on no working directory, which is the property checklist_engine.py:883 actually requires. The guard that failed six times on the pre-fix tree now passes, and a second test pins the committed file to its generator so the paths cannot drift back by hand. One thing the first attempt got wrong and this one fixes: importing the generator from the test wrote a .pyc into examples/, and that .pyc embeds this checkout's absolute path -- the suite was re-creating the very defect inside the directory it was guarding. Bytecode writing is now suppressed for that import.

The demo drives from two unrelated working directories, which is the claim #605 denied. The cwd is genuinely load-bearing and genuinely neutralised: the same spine completed from a /tmp path and from the repo root, and the negative control shows the check still fails when the file is missing. Driving it also surfaced something the handoff only half-anticipated: the workspace writes were never the thing that dirties the tree -- they land in /tmp, outside the repo. What dirties it is the engine writing its own per-run state next to whatever spine it is pointed at, nine files with twelve absolute paths. Those are now ignored in the demo directory, so trying the demo no longer leaves the repo dirty.

An absolute-path guard is blind to a dead RELATIVE path, and the README carried two: the regeneration command pointing into .agent-work/epic-418-followon/ (the generator had moved to .agent-work/archive/), and a recommendation to use scripts/gen_mcp_config.py, which was deleted when per-dispatch identity moved to .mcp.json plus caller-environment expansion. Both were caught by a new guard observed failing on them, not asserted. The guard resolves only tokens rooted at this repo's own top-level entries, so examples/sync-constellation-skills.yml -- a workflow template whose paths deliberately address a CONSUMING repo -- is exempted by name with its reason, and a second test fails if that exemption ever names a file that no longer exists.

Confirmatory layer holds and the map was genuinely stale rather than assumed fresh -- the new generator is a new module, so map/INDEX.md needed the rebuild the handoff warned about. Every new symbol is wired: the generator is not dead code, because the drift test imports it and compares its output to the committed spine, which is also what makes 'generated, not hand-edited' enforceable rather than merely stated.

amendments.reason: The original c3 text ('no workspace writes under examples/') asked the wrong question, and driving the demo proved it. The workspace writes were never the risk -- they land in /tmp. What actually dirties the tracked directory is the ENGINE's own per-run state, written next to whatever spine file it is pointed at: spine.json.journal plus context/g1..g4.json and mechanical/g1..g4.json, nine files carrying twelve absolute-path occurrences. The original check also could not distinguish those from this gate's own intended, staged edits, so it would have failed for the wrong reason. Corrected to the honest question: after a full drive, does anything UNSTAGED or UNTRACKED remain under examples/.
